speaker: UNKNOWN
text: You find something good in there?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Oh, yeah. What are those little guys
up to now?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Two-eighty a ton on the April market.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Oh, in a Cro-Magnon sort of way,
I suppose.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
The Manhattan chapter
of Volunteer Fathers thinks so.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
My size. They felt that and my appearance
might present an inhibiting factor...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...in the development of a healthy
adult-child relationship.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It's not just you. I'm sure every one of us
is influenced by the way we look.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Yeah. And so we all get self-conscious.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Do people do this to you?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I wish people would stop
getting out of my way.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
He told us. It seems that he offered
to be a volunteer father...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Obvious discrimination based on
nothing more than the way he looks.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Yeah. Reminds me of a guy I saw once...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Malcolm the Human Oddity,
they called him.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - He had two complete faces on one head.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Sorry. I didn't mean to gross you out.
I'm sure the other face was a trick.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: It was rubber or putty or something.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Excuse me.
Where's the nearest exit?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
That's right, kid,
but I'm not deaf.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Sorry. I didn't know you
could hear that.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: You know, it must be true...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...that when one sense is lost,
the others become stronger to compensate.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Of course that's true.
For example...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...I can tell that there are four people
at this table.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
One is having a cup of coffee,
two are having a muffin...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Hold it right there, Mr. Foley!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Is that you, officer?
Thank God I found you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Yeah, yeah. Come on. Sorry, Judge Stone.
He keeps trying to escape.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - One of this bunch is a judge?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
All right, so big deal.
So you found me.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You can see.
Where's the sport in that?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I don't know about you,
but I feel lucky...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: And all those great parking places.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I bet they're not crazy about you, either.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Come on. If a fool at the Volunteer Fathers
of America says they don't want you...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It's not just them. People've been making
a big deal out of my size all my life.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
That's why folks started
calling you Bull, huh?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Say, Bull, this is just a thought.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I meant on a regular basis.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Maybe it isn't just your size
that intimidates people.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
If you smile at someone,
they're apt to smile right back at you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Well, you get no argument from me.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Once he stops giving off those menacing
vibes, people will warm up to him.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Of course, these things take time.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: He bared his teeth at me.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Get me out of here, Vince.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I shouldn't have to be subjected to this.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I know, baby. You're an artist.
I love you. Shut up.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Hi there. I'm Harry Stone,
and you are?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Vincent Frago and Iris Keller,
second-degree obscenity.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, these two were apprehended
making a porno flick in Central Park.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Hold on, there, counselor.
The report clearly states that both parties...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...were clothed at the time of arrest.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But before that, they were naked
as jaybirds.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Oh, did I mention I have a witness?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Leonard Bloom, Your Honor.
I saw the whole thing.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Unclothed bodies, writhing around
in the grass...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...contorted dances of lust,
screams of sexual delight.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
So, Mr. Frago, it says here that
you are the producer.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I wear all the creative hats.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I know what you're thinking, Your Honor,
but I'm really a very good actress.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I bet you'd have to be.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: You ever see me in anything?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: No. We spelled "easy" with a Z.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But when my agent called me
about this job...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...he said it was a chance
to do pap in the park.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, I left the background reports
in your office.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Well, go ahead.
Miss Keller and I are discussing...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Once, when I was a kid,
I got mad and broke my baseball bat.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I got mad once and broke my doll.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...I know how much being
a volunteer father meant to you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It would've fulfilled my need
to help others, to become involved...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...to have a positive effect
on the world around me.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Well, there are other organizations
you could join.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Yeah, I tried. The only ones that didn't care
the way I looked were the Marines.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: They just saw me as another shaved head.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Bet it's a snap to dry.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I have to use a chamois.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, I wouldn't be doing my job
if I didn't point out that...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...the pornography case against my clients
is basically circumstantial.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
That's true. It's pretty much
your word against theirs.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Why are you pampering these people?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: The man is a sick dog. Put him away.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
At least I'm not some bluenose hypocrite
who talks real righteous...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...but gets his mail in plain brown wrappers.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Listen, you, I don't have to take
your kind of filth.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Not as much as my fist!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You want him removed
from the courtroom?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
That won't be necessary.
Will it, Mr. Bloom?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I just want the same number of fingers
I came in with.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Thanks a lot, Bull.
I'm glad you were there.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Great job, Bull.
Well, did you see what you just did?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: You were able to be helpful right here.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
No kidding, Bull.
You're a tower of strength.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - "Wall of flesh." Hey, I like that.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
He's got that animal quality
I'm looking for.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
What power! You can take that wimp
Pacino. Give me a big man anytime.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Why don't you all just leave me alone?!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Selma, go see if he's all right.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'll go, but I'm telling you right now,
he's not all right.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Hey, can we hurry this thing up?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Sure. The only way to decide this
is to view the videotape...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...which I will do in the privacy
of my chambers.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: However, I would like both counsel present.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: You're a good man, Harry Stone.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I have never seen Bull like that.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Yes. They can be dangerous
when they're wounded.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But if you can't laugh at other people,
who can you laugh at?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Listen, don't trouble yourself about Bull.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - What do you mean, he's gone?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: He asked me to give you these.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Oh, honey, I don't have the strength to kid.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Did he say where he was going?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
No. He just muttered something about being
fed up with the human race and took off.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Yes. His name is Bull Shannon.
He's a bailiff.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Did anyone down there see him
leave the building?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
If you need a description,
you haven't seen him.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - No one knows where he is?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Is that all you care about, a porno tape?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: What do you mean, about Bull?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Come on. I'm crazy about the big lug.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But there's nothing we can do
until he surfaces.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Besides, as a representative
of the people of New York...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...it is my duty to review all the evidence.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Maybe Bull just needs some time
to think things out, and then he'll be back.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Meantime, there's nothing
we can do but wait.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Well, as long as we're waiting.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But keep in mind that
we're looking at this...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...in terms of the statutory definition
of obscenity...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...and not our own personal
opinions about...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Hey, there's no question about it.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
This one of those blue-jean
commercials?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You'll be able to see him
from your window.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
This window won't open.
Can you see him?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
No. Nothing up there
but a bunch of gargoyles.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Wait. Wait a minute.
One of them's moving.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - I'm not exactly sure what to say.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I wouldn't mention "the bigger they are,
the harder they fall."

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...you're not thinking about
doing anything weird, are you?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I like it up here. Less people.
A man can think.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - I'm not coming down! Leave me alone!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
And calling the Air Force is out.
He'd only swat down their planes.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: No, don't lean over! No! No!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Liz fell down and broke her leg,
and we can't move her.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Would you help, Bull?
She's in a lot of pain.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Will you help us, Bull?
It's pretty bad.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
No, no, no, no, no!
Take the long way.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - What is this place, a maze?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Why can't they make those
"you are here" maps in Braille?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Why don't you just have a seat
right over here.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
What's going on?
You don't look hurt to me.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Bull, I had to talk to you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Don't waste your breath.
It won't affect my decision.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I've decided I'm gonna go away...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...and not associate with any other
human beings as long as I live.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Boy! Now that's what I call a decision.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Where would you go?
I mean, what would you do?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Or I could go up to the North Pole,
one of those radar tracking stations.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I don't care! People won't have to
deal with me.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I won't have to deal with them,
which as far as I'm concerned...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: My name is Foley. Ralph Foley.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You're just gonna walk out
after we've worked together all these...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Bull, we want you to stay.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Okay. If that's the way you feel,
go ahead!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Oh, come on. I was kidding.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Bull, maybe this is
none of my business...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...but frankly, I feel like you're acting
like a little child here.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You're running away
from your problems...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...instead of facing them like a man.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
This is my problem.
How can I run away from that?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Boy, there's one thing I really hate,
it's self-pity.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Hey, before you go away, pal...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...I wanna, I wanna shake your hand.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I never thought I'd meet the man...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...who felt that his problem
was worse than mine.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I thought you were just being
fashionable.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'm afraid Bull doesn't pay much attention
to outward appearances, Mr. Foley.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I get hauled in for shoplifting,
they say:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
"Oh, look at him.
Let the poor blind man go."

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: But in a way, it works for me.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - I had 15 busts, only four convictions.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Boy, Bull sure had this guy pegged.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Yeah, the evidence is all here.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Maybe, but who's gonna send me up?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: That blind stuff didn't work on Bull...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...it doesn't work on me either, right, Bull?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You wanna be treated like a criminal,
Mr. Foley?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I'm gonna send you up for 14 months.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: That's a little rough, isn't it?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Hey, life is rough, isn't it, Bull?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - You're right, Bull. This guy is scum.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I mean, some other judge might give him
probation because he's blind.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You know, take pity. But Bull doesn't have
any pity for him, do you?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
What am I supposed to do, treat him nice?
I mean, remand him into the custody...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Come on. What responsible person
would wanna help out...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...a miserable, rotten, sneaky little
lowlife of a criminal like him?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
If you could see your way clear
to releasing him, Your Honor...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Hey, what the hell is going on
around here?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I don't get a chance all that often...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I guess I know what you mean.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I used to help people too.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But they don't ask me
quite as often anymore.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Come on, judge.
Give the kid a break.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I still got my two weeks' vacation.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Well, okay, but I'd feel better
if you were in a responsible position.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - As of this moment, you're back on the job.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Come on, Ralph. I'll take you home.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: That stuff with me and Ralph...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Oh, yeah?
Hey, mine is stamp collecting.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Really? I'd like to see
your collection sometime.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'm starting to catch on to you,
you know.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I saw those little wheels spinning
in your head.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I knew that you had some kind of plan...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...to bring those two people together
like a human jigsaw puzzle, without ever...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: You know, I was worried about you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...pull any stunt like that again
while I'm around here.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
And don't you ever walk out
and leave me alone on the job.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
And don't you ever forget
that I have the seniority here...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - How about a beer at Muldoon's?
